It should come from the system in that case. Is your `PATH` empty somehow or your bash not available? Strace might help:

```
$ strace -f ./nix-user-chroot ~/.nix bash -c "echo hello world"
```

Bash is in /usr/bin/bash. I tried to put this explicitely in the PATH. Same result. I am a little wary of showing the output of strace because it reveals some information about the layout of our cluster and that could land me in trouble with the company I work for. 

However, it seems that several version of bash are found on the system. The strace has 6-7 lines like:

```
[pid 64881] execve(<redacted path to one version of bash>, ["bash", "-c", "echo hello world"], [/* 62 vars */]) = -1 ENOENT (No such file or directory)
```
that smells like a ld loader issue. maybe the sandbox is preventing .so files from being loaded

It should not shadow `/lib` so. You could try running:

```
./nix-user-chroot ~/.nix ldd /usr/bin/bash
```

Fixed by #121 which reverted back to `pivot_root`.

The root cause was that `chroot()` marks the process as chrooted in the kernel, and `create_user_ns()` refuses `CLONE_NEWUSER` from chrooted processes (to prevent chroot escapes via namespaces). `pivot_root()` properly changes the mount namespace root instead, so the process is not flagged as chrooted and nested user namespaces (bwrap, flatpak, buildFHSEnv, etc.) work again.

Verified on current master:
```
$ nix-user-chroot /tmp/nixdir bwrap --dev-bind / / id
uid=1000(joerg) gid=100(users) ...
```

Note: nested user namespaces (bwrap, flatpak, nested containers) work again since #121, which reverted back to `pivot_root`. The previous `chroot`-based approach caused the kernel to reject `CLONE_NEWUSER` with EPERM (see #57).

The feature request for configurable `uid_map`/`gid_map` is still open — the mappings remain hardcoded to the single-entry identity map `$uid $uid 1`.
